item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.3
item.description:
What is typed into the launcher is no longer lost when it closes.

Added

  • The launcher opens again where it was left. A click elsewhere, or the hotkey pressed again, puts it away as it is: the search, the selected result, what was typed into arguments, a command that is open. Opened again within a minute, it shows what it did. Settings → General sets how long, from never to always. Escape and ⌘W still close it for good.
  • ↑ in the empty search brings back what was searched for before, newest first, with what was typed into a quicklink's arguments and the result that was selected. ↑ and ↓ then go through the earlier searches until something is typed; ⌃N and ⌃P move the selection meanwhile. A search is remembered when it is run, cleared with Escape, or closed with ⌘W, and the same search is listed once. Settings → General sets how many are kept, the last 100 unless chosen otherwise, and clears them.

Changed

  • Files that were found stay listed while the same search is looked up again, as when an application was installed meanwhile, instead of going and coming back.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.2
item.description:
Where the keyboard is in the launcher, which the first testers found unreliable.

Fixed

  • The launcher puts the keyboard into the field of the screen it shows and keeps it there, instead of leaving that to how soon macOS moves focus to a field that has just appeared. This covers opening the launcher right after closing it, opening the clipboard history, the quicklinks or another command with its hotkey, and renaming a pinned entry of the clipboard history.
  • Going back to a list, as from editing a quicklink or from what uninstalling an application would remove, puts the keyboard into its filter again. Before, typing did nothing until the filter was clicked.
  • In the quicklink editor, Tab goes from the link back to the name. Before, it left the keyboard with neither. Editing a quicklink puts the insertion point at the end of its link instead of selecting all of it.
  • Typing is never lost to a launcher that is open: should the keyboard be with no field at all, the first key puts it back where it belongs.

item.title: 0.1.0-alpha.1
item.description:
The first public alpha.

Included

  • An app icon made in Icon Composer, with a matching template icon in the menu bar.
  • A disk image to download, with Inky and the Applications folder to drag it onto.
  • Updates from GitHub Releases through Sparkle, with a signed feed and archives, for signed and notarized downloads. Every version is a download; Settings → General picks the Stable or the Beta update channel, and a pre-release starts on Beta. About and the update window show the whole version, such as 0.1.0-alpha.1.
  • A welcome window on first launch for the hotkey, features, clipboard history and its permissions, online lookups and startup.
  • Application launching, fuzzy search, usage ranking and Spotlight file search.
  • Quicklinks with arguments, clipboard and selected-text placeholders.
  • Clipboard history for text, images and files, with pins and retention settings. Copies that password managers mark as confidential are left out by default.
  • Calculator, unit and currency conversions, time queries and color conversion.
  • System commands, per-command hotkeys, disabled commands and configurable fallbacks.
  • Application uninstall review with selected files moved to the Trash.
  • MIT source license, GeoNames attribution, contribution and security policies, and macOS test/build CI.

Fixed during release preparation

  • Failed clipboard database opens preserve saved databases, journals and images; a visible temporary history is used until the problem is resolved.
  • Clipboard text containing embedded null characters is preserved when copied again.
  • Uninstalling revalidates selected files against the current application inventory, rejecting unrelated files and data now shared by another installed copy.
  • Failed GeoNames regeneration no longer truncates the bundled city list.
  • Time arithmetic rejects durations that overflow or produce dates outside years 1–9999.

Known limitations

  • Requires a Mac with Apple silicon; Intel Macs are not supported.
  • Clipboard history is stored without application-level encryption. Passwords copied from apps that do not mark them as confidential are kept. Disable the module if needed.
  • Builds from source use an ad-hoc signature and do not update themselves. Signed, notarized, self-updating downloads start with this version.
  • Application-data matching for uninstalling is heuristic; review the selected files.
  • Currency conversions may use stale cached reference rates.
  • Lua extensions are planned and cannot be installed yet.
